macro_context.h8_summary: Peak-to-fade. Small-bank funding peaked mid-July, TGA drain active, 3 FOMC dissents for a hike.

small_bank_credit.summary: Reserves thinned from $509B as TGA drain hit small-bank cushions through July.
small_bank_credit.detail:
Your credit union sits in the small-bank tier the H.8 tracks weekly. Through July, that tier's funding health went from 'strongest in the dataset' to 'adequate but starting to fade.' Core deposits accreted while CDs declined — institutions like yours paying competitive checking rates to keep relationship money. Your 4% APY is that story, in your statement.

The TGA reserve drain starting late July thinned small-bank cash cushions from $509B to $487B; your credit union's reserves thinned with the system. Your 3.75% mortgage, meanwhile, is entirely insulated from current rate movements — locked and getting more valuable every time market rates rise.

reads.economy: Your household ran a $1,274 surplus in July — 12.7% of income retained. Spending rate of 87.3% means for every dollar earned, 87 cents went out the door. The 10.6% savings rate (investment transfers) is the growth engine — that capital compounds independently of your earned income. Debt service at 8.9% of income ($897/month across Lake Trust, Synchrony, Citibank, Chase) is the rate-sensitive line: if the Fed hikes in September, variable-rate balances cost more immediately. Your mortgage payment is fixed and doesn't move. The forward question is whether income holds steady — July NFP at −23K suggests the labor market is softening, and any disruption to either income stream would compress the surplus quickly at this spending rate.
reads.savings: Your checking earns 4.00% APY — nearly matching the 1Y Treasury at 4.05%. With CPI at 3.4%, your real yield is +0.6%: purchasing power is growing, barely. Your credit union is doing exactly what the H.8 showed small banks doing in July — paying competitive rates on core deposits to retain relationship money rather than relying on expensive wholesale funding. That 4% rate is the consumer-facing side of the deposit competition story. As long as the Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, this rate holds. The three hawkish FOMC dissents in July are actually favorable for your APY — if they hike, your variable rate likely moves up. The risk is the other direction: when cuts eventually come, this drops first.
reads.mortgage: Your 3.75% fixed rate, locked in September 2019, sits nearly 3 percentage points below today's ~6.6% market rate. This is one of the most valuable financial positions you hold. Each month, $253 of your $603 P&I goes to principal — building equity at a borrowing cost that would run roughly $615/month in interest alone at current origination rates. Refinancing destroys value here; you hold this rate until maturity or until market rates drop well below 3.75%, which the current Fed posture makes unlikely. The $600 escrow covers property tax, FHA mortgage insurance ($79/month), and hazard insurance. The FHA MIP is a cost you carry for the life of this loan — but at 3.75% vs 6.6%, absorbing the MIP is still the right trade.
reads.spending:
Top 2 discretionary categories to watch:

1. Groceries — $1,000. Walmart and Walmart.com account for ~$580 of this. Aldi runs $249 and consistently undercuts Walmart by 15–25% on staples. Shifting $200/month of Walmart grocery spend to Aldi could save $40–50/month without changing what you buy. At $50 saved, your monthly surplus rises from $1,274 to $1,324.

2. Dining — $480. Spread across 30+ transactions — frequent $5–15 stops (McDonald's, Panera, Starbucks, Taco Bell, Jimmy Johns) rather than a few large meals. Coffee alone (Starbucks + coffeeshops) runs ~$50/month. Cutting frequency by one-third — roughly 10 fewer stops — saves ~$100/month. At $100 saved, your surplus rises from $1,274 to $1,374.

Combined potential: $150/month, or $1,800/year redirected to savings or debt paydown.

reads.monthly_note:
July 2026 was the month the small-bank funding story peaked and began to turn. Your credit union — a small financial institution in the Taylor, MI area — captured that arc.

Through mid-July, the H.8 showed the healthiest small-bank funding picture in the dataset: core deposits accreting, borrowings at record lows ($280.5B), cash cushions at multi-month highs. Your 4.00% checking APY is the consumer-facing expression of that health — credit unions competing for relationship deposits by paying near-Treasury rates on liquid accounts. With CPI at 3.4%, your real yield is a slim but positive 0.6%.

The turn came in the back half of the month. Treasury began building its cash balance toward the $950B QRA target, draining reserves from the banking system. Small-bank cash dropped from $509B mid-month to $487B by month-end. The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% on July 29, but three regional presidents dissented for a hike — the most hawkish signal since 2016. September hike odds hit 63%.

Your mortgage at 3.75% is the anchor of the household balance sheet. Originated in 2019 at $130K, now at $111,766 — you've paid down $18,333 in principal over nearly seven years. At current market rates near 6.6%, this loan would cost roughly $615/month in interest alone versus your $349. That spread is locked wealth. The escrow ($600/month) covers property tax, FHA insurance, and hazard insurance — costs that rise with assessments and premiums, not with the Fed.

Two income streams brought in roughly $9,328 in regular deposits against $8,784 in total outflows. The $986 flowing to investment accounts is a 10.6% savings rate — meaningful capital accumulation. Debt service at $897/month (Lake Trust, Synchrony, Citibank, Chase) is the rate-sensitive line item: if the Fed hikes in September, variable-rate balances cost more immediately. Your mortgage doesn't move.

The forward read: your household is positioned well for a rate-hold or hike environment. The 3.75% mortgage gets more valuable as market rates rise. The 4% checking APY could increase with a hike. The vulnerability is on the debt service side — credit card and consumer loan rates rise — and on the employment side, where July NFP at −23K suggests hiring has paused. Watch whether August and September employment data confirm that softening.
